intelligence.essence: Volume-Adaptive Alert Calibration Law: NayaNET shall calibrate statistical alert thresholds using effective independent sample size, traffic variability, observable effect coverage, and operational risk. It shall control false alarms across repeated tests and the provider fleet, rather than per observation alone. Statistical thresholds may govern investigation urgency but may never override independently established safety violations. Provider guarantees and execution authority remain separately qualified. The practical result: low volume — 'we do not have enough observations to conclude drift; reconcile and keep testing'; bursty — 'one correlated rate-limit incident, not hundreds of independent contract failures'; high volume — 'statistically detectable but only materially consequential changes escalate urgently'; any volume with verified duplicates — 'the guarantee is withdrawn immediately.' Same safety standard everywhere; different statistical methods per regime; safety findings never wait for sample sizes.
intelligence.falsifier: One percentage threshold applied to every provider; percent-change alerts on tiny denominators; correlated burst failures counted as independent confirmations; tiny significant fluctuations paged at high volume; a confirmed duplicate waiting for statistical significance; baselines contaminated with unresolved incidents; thresholds tuned to perfection on the same historical incidents then called validated; a traffic-profile change silently altering evidence standards or LAW permissions; repeated peeking without anytime-valid correction; availability metrics presented as contract-correctness evidence.

human_view.meaning: Same safety bar for everyone, different math for different traffic. A quiet provider with five requests a week can't be judged by the same ruler as one doing thousands a day — one timeout out of five is 20%, but it proves almost nothing, and the statistics must say so honestly. A bursty provider that fails 500 times in one quota incident had ONE incident, not 500 independent contract breaches. A high-volume provider will make every tiny wiggle 'statistically significant' — so we require the wiggle to actually matter before anyone gets woken up. And none of this statistics machinery ever gets a vote on a proven double-effect: one verified duplicate pulls the guarantee immediately, at any volume, no sample-size minimum. The fleet gets a false-alarm budget spent across all endpoints and all time — because a hundred 1%-tests means a false alarm is more likely than not. Baselines learn only from clean history, threshold changes run in shadow mode first, and no traffic change ever silently rewrites what counts as proof. The four sentences the system must be able to say: 'not enough data — keep testing'; 'one incident, not hundreds'; 'detectable but not consequential'; and 'duplicate verified — guarantee withdrawn.'

intelligence.learning_lesson: This is the statistical conscience the alerting stack needed: AER-ALERT-1 sets the ladder; AER-CAL-1 calibrates the rungs. The permanent contributions: the three-regime strategy selector, the safety-vs-statistical separation (safety findings never wait for n), the effective-sample-size discipline with the zero-failure upper-bound table, the fleet-wide α-budget with the 63% lesson, the paired-windows method, the materiality conjunction, the replay-calibration protocol with sealed fixtures A/B/C, and the feedback-loop prevention (admissible-period baselines, shadow mode, versioned profiles). Every future monitoring threshold inherits this: calibrate to the regime, control the fleet, and never let statistics overrule a proven violation.

naya_view.directive: Select statistical methods by effective independent sample size, variability, and risk — never raw traffic alone. Keep safety findings independent of sample size; let statistics govern investigation urgency only. Use exact methods for small samples; cluster-aware models for correlated traffic; sequential methods for high-volume stability; anytime-valid inference for repeated monitoring. Budget false alarms across the fleet and across time. Require materiality alongside statistical signal for operational pages. Calibrate by historical replay with sealed held-out fixtures; prevent feedback loops with admissible-period baselines and shadow mode. Version every profile; never let recalibration silently alter evidence standards or LAW permissions.
